title: Safe Join
statement: Implement `solve(base, name)`. `base` and `name` are POSIX-style paths using `/`. Join `name` onto `base` and return the normalized path only when it stays inside `base`. If `name` is absolute or the result escapes `base` with `..`, return the string `error`. Normalization uses lexical `.` and `..` only. Do not touch the filesystem.
hints: Reject a name that starts with /.
Split the joined path and apply . and .. lexically.
The result must equal base or have base plus a slash as a prefix of a segment boundary, not a string prefix of a sibling folder.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Path traversal is a join that leaves the root you intended.

editorial: Path traversal is a join that leaves the root you intended. Lexical normalization resolves .. before you check the prefix. A string startswith is not enough if base is /var/app and the result is /var/apple. Compare path segments.
